title: Alert fires and notifications
description: Firing and pending Prometheus alerts with the time they entered that state, the Email or SMS route, and Alertmanager delivery counters for email and the SMS webhook.

panels.title: Current alerts
panels.description: Snapshot of Prometheus alerts. The time picker does not filter this row.

panels.title: Firing
panels.description: Alerts in firing state. Filtered by Job, Priority, Alert, Server, and Owner.

panels.title: Pending
panels.description: Alerts still inside the rule for-duration. Not notified yet.

panels.title: P0 firing
panels.description: Firing P0 alerts. Alertmanager route sms-email-p0 sends Email and SMS.

panels.title: P2 firing
panels.description: Firing P2 alerts. Alertmanager route email-p2 sends Email only.

panels.title: Oldest firing
panels.description: Earliest ALERTS_FOR_STATE among firing alerts in the current filter. This is when that alert entered firing.

panels.title: Posted to Alertmanager
panels.description: Prometheus notifications posted to http://127.0.0.1:9093 during the selected time range. Not an email or SMS count, and not filtered by the alert variables.

panels.title: Email and SMS delivery
panels.description: Alertmanager counters. Empty until Prometheus scrapes job alertmanager on 127.0.0.1:9093.

panels.title: Email attempts
panels.description: alertmanager_notification_requests_total for integration email over the selected time range. One request is one SMTP send, not one alert row.

panels.title: SMS attempts
panels.description: alertmanager_notification_requests_total for integration webhook. In this Alertmanager config the webhook is the SMS gateway.

panels.title: Email failed
panels.description: Failed email notification requests in the selected time range. Missing scrape is Not scraped, not zero.

panels.title: SMS failed
panels.description: Failed webhook (SMS gateway) notification requests in the selected time range.

panels.title: Firing alerts by priority
panels.description: Current firing series over time. A series disappears when the alert resolves.

panels.title: Prometheus to Alertmanager
panels.description: Rate of notification posts, errors, and drops for the local Alertmanager. This is the handoff, not email or SMS.

panels.title: Email and SMS request rate
panels.description: Alertmanager notification request rate. SMS is the webhook integration. No data until job alertmanager is scraped.

panels.title: Failed email and SMS
panels.description: alertmanager_notifications_failed_total by integration and reason.

panels.title: Alerts, fire time, and notify route
Alerts by name
panels.description: One row per alert name and route. State since is the oldest and newest ALERTS_FOR_STATE in that group. Notify route is the Alertmanager route: P0 and P1 are Email + SMS, P2 is Email. This is the configured route, not a per-alert delivery receipt.

targets.expr: count by (alertname, job, priority, severity, owner, notify, alertstate) (label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(ALERTS_FOR_STATE{job=~"$job",priority=~"$priority",alertname=~"$alertname",instance=~"$instance",owner=~"$owner"} * ignoring(alertstate) group_left(alertstate) ALERTS{alertstate=~"$state",job=~"$job",priority=~"$priority",alertname=~"$alertname",instance=~"$instance",owner=~"$owner"},"notify","Email + SMS","priority","^(P0|P1)$"),"notify","Email","priority","^P2$"),"notify","Email","notify","^$"))

min by (alertname, job, priority, severity, owner, notify, alertstate) (label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(ALERTS_FOR_STATE{job=~"$job",priority=~"$priority",alertname=~"$alertname",instance=~"$instance",owner=~"$owner"} * ignoring(alertstate) group_left(alertstate) ALERTS{alertstate=~"$state",job=~"$job",priority=~"$priority",alertname=~"$alertname",instance=~"$instance",owner=~"$owner"},"notify","Email + SMS","priority","^(P0|P1)$"),"notify","Email","priority","^P2$"),"notify","Email","notify","^$")) * 1000

max by (alertname, job, priority, severity, owner, notify, alertstate) (label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(ALERTS_FOR_STATE{job=~"$job",priority=~"$priority",alertname=~"$alertname",instance=~"$instance",owner=~"$owner"} * ignoring(alertstate) group_left(alertstate) ALERTS{alertstate=~"$state",job=~"$job",priority=~"$priority",alertname=~"$alertname",instance=~"$instance",owner=~"$owner"},"notify","Email + SMS","priority","^(P0|P1)$"),"notify","Email","priority","^P2$"),"notify","Email","notify","^$")) * 1000

panels.title: Firing and pending alerts
panels.description: Each active alert series. State since is when it entered the current state. For firing, that is the fire time, after the rule for duration. Extra labels such as volume or database stay visible. Resolved alerts are not listed.

panels.title: Delivery evidence in the selected time range
Notification requests
panels.description: Attempted and failed Alertmanager notification requests. receiver_name is present only when Alertmanager is started with receiver names in metrics. Webhook is the SMS gateway.

panels.title: Failed notifications by reason
panels.description: Individual notification failures, which can be higher than request failures when one request carries many alerts.

options.content:
### What each number means
- **State since** comes from `ALERTS_FOR_STATE`. For a firing row, that is when the alert fired.
- **Notify route** follows Alertmanager: P0 `sms-email-p0` and P1 `email-sms-p1` are Email + SMS. P2 `email-p2` is Email only. SMS is the webhook receiver, not a native SMS integration.
- That route is configuration. Alertmanager does not store which alert produced which email or SMS. Delivery panels are counters for the whole selected time range.
- **Posted to Alertmanager** is Prometheus handing alert groups to `127.0.0.1:9093`. It is not proof that SMTP or the SMS gateway accepted them.
- Email and SMS panels stay **Not scraped** until Prometheus scrapes job `alertmanager` on `127.0.0.1:9093`. A reload of Prometheus is required after that job is added. Do not read an empty panel as zero sends.
- The alert tables are the current snapshot. Resolved alerts leave the list. The time picker applies to delivery counters and trend charts.
